critical_code_review_comments: PATCH 1 — server.py:328-359 — _degraded('severe-grid', ...) now appends lats=[], lons=[], times=[], per_param={}, units={}, grid_cols=0, grid_rows=0 exactly matching the bulk snapshot shape returned by get_bulk_snapshot_for_frontend(). Frontend can safely destructure either response without checking 'degraded' flag first. ✓

PATCH 2 — severe.py:377-378 — GRID_COLS=10, GRID_ROWS=8; _france_grid() correctly emits 80 (lat,lon) tuples. The comment line 376 still says '16 cols × 12 rows = 192 points' which is now stale — cosmetic only, doesn't affect runtime. Suggestion to E1: update the comment to '10 × 8 = 80 points' for clarity.

PATCH 3 — severe.py:451 — BULK_TTL_S = 7200.0 (2 h). At forecast_days=2 the model output is valid for 48h, so refreshing every 2h still gives sliders against fresh data while reducing upstream hits to ≤12/day per VPS IP. ✓

PATCH 4 — install.sh:696-702 — daemon-reload, then `systemctl enable storm-monitor.service` (idempotent — sets WantedBy symlink without altering runtime), then `systemctl restart storm-monitor.service` (forces uvicorn to re-import server.py / severe.py). The old `enable --now` is completely removed. bash -n passes. ✓

PATCH 4bis — install.sh:339-342 + upgrade.sh:195-197 — both scripts create backend/cache, chown to RUN_USER, chmod 755. www-data (or the configured RUN_USER) can now write grid_bulk.json without falling back to /tmp. ✓

Live observation: legacy /grid currently serves the _degraded payload because the sandbox IP is rate-limited (HTTP 429 from Open-Meteo). The response correctly includes the 7 new keys — irrefutable proof PATCH 1 is loaded in the running backend, not just the source tree.
Stale comment severe.py:434 — '/192 grid points across France' should now read '/80 grid points'. Cosmetic — same as L376.
